status: active authority convention and planned interface contracts
authority: Completed, accepted code modules and the assembled accepted codebase are the primary source of truth for implemented behavior and supported interfaces at their exact accepted revision. The atlas and active standards retain intended requirements and acceptance obligations. Current comment stubs establish locations and proposals only; scoped observations are not completion admission.

sections.title: Meaning of a publicly accessible interface
sections.body: Every module must present a documented, discoverable, versioned interface to its named consumers. Public means supported consumer access: an internal Rust facade, Julia API, CLI, typed tool action, local Unix socket, stdio exchange or package schema. It does not require exposing private helpers or adding TCP/HTTP listeners. Use the minimum language visibility that makes the supported boundary callable. External Rust crate consumers require an accessible library target and re-export path; the current binary/comment stubs do not provide one. Julia exported/public names and docstrings describe supported use; exports do not isolate code. Exact symbols and host registration signatures must be chosen and tested during authorized implementation, then reflected from accepted source.

sections.title: Authority follows accepted implementation
sections.body: Lifecycle: planned_stub → implementation_candidate → accepted_module. Packaging and deployment are separate observations; accepted does not imply installed. A candidate may become accepted only through an admitted completion record binding module ID, source/test/fixture/dependency/toolchain digests, public-interface and migration identities, applicable task and standard revisions, full ≥50-case/zero-warning qualification, assimilation/mutation evidence, integration/security dispositions and owner/reviewer admission. Source changes invalidate applicability until re-admitted. The assembled codebase requires its own integrated release acceptance; a sum of module results or child successes cannot substitute. No admission collector is implemented in this documentation tooling; accepted_interfaces is empty and must remain empty until a separately verified admission path exists.

sections.title: Resolve divergence without rewriting facts
sections.body: For accepted code, publish current interface facts from its exact source/schema/migration subject and keep desired changes alongside them. A defect remains a defect even if code exhibits it. Requirements, security constraints and testing floors are not weakened to match a failing implementation. Record current-versus-desired drift, affected callers/callees, change owner, repair or explicitly authorized requirement revision, and re-verification. Never generate runtime code from a stale atlas, infer acceptance from filesystem presence, or silently edit a released migration. Historical source captures and receipts retain their original bytes and scope.

sections.title: Required contract fields for every supported entry point
sections.body: Before acceptance record: stable interface and operation ID; owner and intended audience; source symbol/schema path; signature and typed input/output schema with examples; errors and unknown-effect semantics; capabilities and credential custody; maximum sizes, queue/backpressure and deadline; idempotency key/replay/readback; cancellation and settlement; concurrency and workspace/resource ownership; compatibility/deprecation range; evidence and diagnostic references; exact admitted revision. Reuse the existing numbered APIs, IPC and actions. The per-module operations below are semantic design obligations, not newly invented callable symbols. Their mapped API/action notes supply existing detailed protocol contracts. Any missing concrete field blocks interface acceptance.

sections.title: Discoverability, documentation and compatibility gates
sections.body: Rust modules need rustdoc for the supported facade, examples and caller compile checks across admitted targets/features; where rustdoc or other applicable checks emit baseline warnings/errors, qualification fails. Julia needs supported entry-point docstrings, deliberate exports or version-appropriate public declarations, contract examples and qualified package loading. CLI/actions need help/inspect output, input/result/error schemas and literal-value examples that agree across CLI, UDS and tool projections. Bash, Pi, skills and workflows need versioned manifest/entry-point and compatibility documentation. Private implementation details stay private. Check both directions of each integration: caller assumptions and callee guarantees, returned evidence/error/usage and cancellation. A breaking change requires explicit version/migration and affected-consumer testing.

sections.title: Local transport and capability boundaries
sections.body: Keep each existing IPC endpoint under its declared lifecycle owner and custody. Public documentation does not authorize a world-readable/writable Unix socket, worker access to the operator socket, or Internet service. Any future transport addition requires a separate accepted contract for bind identity, authentication/authorization, credentials, resource limits, failure/readback and deployment evidence. Current interface mappings remain proposals; no listener, RPC or service is installed by this corpus update.

sections.title: Update loop and proof of completion
sections.body: Inspect exact candidate and accepted revision → compare requirements and interface contracts → implement only authorized changes → execute relevant checks → retain independently collected observations → repair/escalate → reverify → obtain completion admission → project current code facts into atlas/vault/ultra map and master indexes → publish with matching hashes and live link readback. Preserve current and desired views separately. Until the admission collector exists, corpus-sync can verify navigation, hashes and declared observation consistency only. Documentation completion must never be reported as module or release completion.

modules.surface: Rust types and validation facade shared by declared consumers; serializable boundary schemas through existing APIs.

operations.inputs: Schema version; task, attempt, generation, caller and correlation identities; bounded payload

operations.inputs: Producer/consumer version and declared capabilities
operations.outputs: Supported subset or explicit incompatibility

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound lengths, integer ranges and enum variants; reject missing identity and ambiguous encodings before effects. Unknown versions are not guessed.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Pure constructors/validation. No database, grants, process control or state acceptance. Changes propagate to all wire consumers through explicit compatibility review.
modules.required_proof: Round-trip and malformed schema cases; old/new consumer fixtures; non-lossy error and identity projection; fuzz/property campaign on parsing bounds.

modules.surface: Rust task coordinator facade; operator and tool access exclusively through admitted actions and app transports.

operations.inputs: Caller capability, task specification, acceptance revision, limits and idempotency key
operations.outputs: Preview exclusions or durable task/attempt identity and initial state

operations.inputs: Task identity; bounded listing cursor or cancellation request
operations.outputs: Committed snapshot/page or acknowledged cancellation obligation

operations.inputs: Expected generation, observed worker/checker facts, explicit operator resolution authority
operations.outputs: Committed transition with evidence links or conflict/denial

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound task/attempt counts and deadlines. Refuse stale generations, incompatible retry bodies and missing grants. Cancellation acknowledgement is not process settlement.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Owns the plan/execute/observe/verify/repair/close loop. Mutations commit through store with conservative budget and retained uncertainty; checker evidence alone does not grant acceptance.
modules.required_proof: Boundary acceptance, duplicate submission, lost reply/readback, stale result, verify-repair-verify loop, cancellation and exhausted-budget cases.

modules.surface: Rust ledger transaction facade; SQL files form a versioned schema boundary owned by store, with no direct consumer SQL writes.

operations.inputs: Expected state/generation, task/attempt facts, reservation deltas, evidence references and outbox events
operations.outputs: Atomic commit identity and sequence or conflict with no partial effect

operations.inputs: Bounded identifiers, cursor, snapshot requirements
operations.outputs: Typed rows/events with ledger epoch and pagination

operations.inputs: Exclusive writer custody, ordered migration identity/checksum and supported version range
operations.outputs: Transactional schema transition or refusal; independently read-back version and integrity

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound transactions and busy retry windows. Surface disk full, corruption, constraint failure and unsupported schema explicitly; never turn a failed write into success.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Single logical ledger writer; transactions maintain cross-table invariants and durable outbox. Released migration bytes are immutable. Replay uses durable identities.
modules.required_proof: Atomicity and crash recovery; foreign-key/uniqueness constraints; concurrent starters; fresh install/upgrade/restore; migration checksum mismatch and schema readback.

modules.surface: Rust roster queries and controlled updates; roster actions are the public projection for model, agent and service records.

operations.inputs: Kind, constraints, locality, version, bounded page and observation cutoff
operations.outputs: Declared/observed records with freshness, provenance and explicit unknowns

operations.inputs: Caller grant, stable record ID, expected revision and validated change
operations.outputs: New roster revision or conflict/denial

operations.inputs: Registered owner identity and approved probe observation
operations.outputs: Dated useful-health observation without acquiring lifecycle authority

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound records and cache age; duplicate IDs, unsupported capability claims and stale observations remain visible.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Updates preserve revisions. Discovery cannot grant control, manufacture health or imply that a model is installed or eligible.
modules.required_proof: Fresh/stale/unknown separation; capability filtering; concurrent update conflicts; disabled record exclusion; spoofed service/model identity refusal.

modules.surface: Pure Rust eligibility/ranking facade used by task; no independent routing daemon or new public endpoint.

operations.inputs: Task class, constraints, roster snapshot, budget and admitted policy revision
operations.outputs: Eligible recipes and explicit exclusions

operations.inputs: Eligible set, dated measured observations and deterministic tie policy
operations.outputs: Chosen model/effort/adapter recipe, reasons, uncertainty and fallback order

operations.inputs: Failure category, remaining resources and previous attempt identity
operations.outputs: Permitted next recipe or truthful refusal

modules.errors_and_limits: No eligible candidate is a normal refusal. Missing measurements stay unknown. Bound search and require deterministic replay inputs.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: No dispatch or budget mutation. Julia recommendations are candidates until admitted; baseline survives invalid or stale challengers.
modules.required_proof: Eligibility invariants; dominated/unsupported model refusal; stable tie-breaks; stale evaluation, constrained fallback and cost/failure-inclusive comparison.

modules.surface: Rust reservation and accounting facade integrated with task/store; typed usage reports from workers/checkers/context/cohorts.

operations.inputs: Task/attempt/parent allocation, unit-labelled upper bounds and expected revision
operations.outputs: Admitted reservation identity or refusal

operations.inputs: Reservation ID, observed usage provenance, uncertainty and worker settlement
operations.outputs: Conservative balance, discrepancy and unresolved liability

operations.inputs: Task/thread scope and observation revision
operations.outputs: Bounded available, reserved, spent and unknown totals

modules.errors_and_limits: Reject negative/nonfinite/incompatible units and overflow. Unknown usage is not zero; insufficient budget is explicit.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Atomic conservation across concurrent parent/child requests; release only with required settlement proof. Retried reports are idempotent by identity.
modules.required_proof: Conservation properties; concurrency; retries and delayed usage; compaction/checker costs; abandoned work and uncertain cancellation liability.

modules.surface: Rust adapter facade over bounded Pi/native/inference protocols; no access to the operator control socket by default.

operations.inputs: Attempt/generation, exact recipe, scoped workspace, limits, credentials and cancellation channel
operations.outputs: Start acknowledgement, actual runtime/model identity and capability limits

operations.inputs: Framed ordered adapter messages tied to the admitted attempt
operations.outputs: Activity, usage, candidate artifact references and classified exit

operations.inputs: Attempt/process identity, deadline and cancellation reason
operations.outputs: Cancellation acknowledgement, process/workspace settlement proof or explicit unknown

modules.errors_and_limits: Frame/stream/size/time bounds and schema negotiation; malformed, duplicated, stale or spoofed messages cannot close a task.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: One adapter owns its process lifecycle under coordinator custody. Candidate output is untrusted and never checker evidence. Lost replies require identity readback.
modules.required_proof: Pi/native protocol fixtures; launch failures; partial frames; wrong actual model; cancellation races; residual writable process and hostile output isolation.

modules.surface: Rust verifier facade operating on protected fixtures and the exact candidate subject; evidence consumers are task/release admission.

operations.inputs: Acceptance revision, source/artifact subject, admitted fixture and toolchain identities
operations.outputs: Bounded verification plan with independent oracle and collector custody

operations.inputs: Exact execution outputs, profiles, case identities and diagnostics
operations.outputs: Per-criterion pass/fail/invalid/unmeasured observations with raw references

operations.inputs: Observation set, module standard and integration obligations
operations.outputs: Coverage/subject/diagnostic/assimilation/mutation gaps and candidate disposition

modules.errors_and_limits: Wrong-subject, zero-execution, skipped, stale and forged observations cannot pass. Baseline warnings/errors must be zero.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Checker cannot accept its own task or trust worker-authored receipts. Protected output capture and tests are isolated from candidate write authority.
modules.required_proof: Forged result and fixture tamper detectors; wrong subject/profile; meaningful 50-case accounting; intended-fault plus benign mirror; full-standard collector qualification remains future work.

modules.surface: Rust reconciliation facade called by task/app on restart, timeout and uncertain effects.

operations.inputs: Ledger epoch, active attempts, process/session identities and workspace claims
operations.outputs: Reconciliation candidates with custody and uncertainty

operations.inputs: Trusted process/readback observations and bounded cancellation policy
operations.outputs: Settled obligations, pending cleanup or explicit ambiguity

operations.inputs: Committed outbox/event identities and restore epoch
operations.outputs: Replay plan without repeating accepted engine effects

modules.errors_and_limits: PID alone is insufficient identity. Missing process visibility, lease expiry and timeout cannot establish safe workspace reuse.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Acts through registered lifecycle owners; retains cleanup obligations until verified. Restoration changes epochs and rejects stale observations.
modules.required_proof: Crash/restart, PID reuse, partial cleanup, restored epoch, late result, lost acknowledgement and retained reservation cases.

modules.surface: Rust orchestration facade for specialist threads, assignments, resource claims and parent joins; thread read actions project state.

operations.inputs: Parent acceptance, finite child DAG, roles, revisions, budgets and resource claims
operations.outputs: Thread/assignment identities and explicit dependencies

operations.inputs: Thread/cursor and child observations tied to current assignment
operations.outputs: Bounded state, evidence, dissent and unresolved gaps

operations.inputs: Required child criteria, context revisions, conflict and final-verifier disposition
operations.outputs: Parent integration candidate, repair plan or blocked join

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound concurrency, fan-out, token/time budgets and retries. Detect cycles, stale briefs, duplicate ownership and write conflicts.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: One coordinator owns assignment/join; child success never accepts parent. Shared allocation is conserved and workspaces follow explicit custody.
modules.required_proof: Disjoint work synergy; stale brief; overlapping writes; missing child; contradictory evidence; dissent preservation; failed join repair and final integrated verification.

modules.surface: Rust bounded context packet facade; consumers are cohort, task and declared skill/worker integration paths.

operations.outputs: Selected references, bounded content, omissions, source and relationship gaps

operations.inputs: Old/new source revisions, permitted scope and stable context identity
operations.outputs: Change/provenance report with affected consumers

operations.inputs: Measured selection/compaction work and usage provenance
operations.outputs: Usage fact for budget accounting

modules.errors_and_limits: Untrusted source instructions do not grant actions. Bound expansion, path access, recursion and packet size; failed fetches remain gaps.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Read scoped sources; preserve provenance and bidirectional dependency/return context. No silent expansion of access or evidence authority.
modules.required_proof: Budget cutoffs; stale source; omitted dependency; prompt-injection boundary; denied path; reproducible packet ordering and cost inclusion.

modules.surface: Rust committed-event subscription/delivery facade; events.subscribe is the declared consumer action.

operations.inputs: Caller visibility, bounded cursor, epoch and backlog limit
operations.outputs: Ordered permitted event stream plus gap/resync indication

operations.inputs: Committed event ID, recipient identity and durable delivery key
operations.outputs: Delivery receipt or pending retry with failure category

operations.inputs: Event/recipient identity and observation cutoff
operations.outputs: Delivered/pending/unknown state without task-state invention

modules.errors_and_limits: Bound queues and replay windows; slow consumers receive backpressure or resumable gaps. Invalid/restored epoch requires resync.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Outbox begins after ledger commit. Delivery retry never reruns task effects; dedup uses durable event/recipient identity.
modules.required_proof: Commit-before-delivery; lost ack, replay dedup, cursor expiry, restored epoch, slow subscriber and visibility filtering.

modules.surface: Rust useful-health and delegated lifecycle facade, projected by service.inspect/probe/action.

modules.errors_and_limits: Probe bounds include time/resource/network scope. Discovery does not authorize start/stop. Lost reply is not permission to repeat a destructive effect.
modules.effects_and_concurrency: Lifecycle ownership remains with the registered binary/daemon/systemd/external owner; service is an adapter, not another supervisor.
modules.required_proof: Unauthorized probe/action refusal; wrong unit/owner; lost response readback; apparently live but useless health; replay and conflicting action identity.

operations.inputs: Last cursor/epoch and task identity

operations.outputs: Report/artifact identity, measured cost, uncertainty and classified failure

operations.outputs: Accepted-for-review candidate or rejection preserving current baseline
